# IceCube: Catching Cosmic Messengers from Antarctica

Buried beneath nearly a mile of Antarctic ice, about 100 holes contain basketball-sized light detectors that capture ghostly cosmic particles called neutrinos—invisible messengers shot across the universe from exploding stars and other violent cosmic events. When these high-energy neutrinos smash into ice molecules, they create a faint blue glow that the frozen detectors catch, allowing scientists to eavesdrop on the universe's most dramatic events from the most remote place on Earth.
